analyst_view.overall: Early view: Hamburg have turned their season around under Merlin Polzin after losing their first three games, swapping possession play for a compact, low-possession set-up, though captain Nicolai Remberg is out long term after ACL surgery. Schalke sit 17th, lost in Hoffenheim on 8 November after a Loris Karius error, and lost Robin Gosens to a knee injury and Timo Becker to a foot injury; this is refreshed with team news the day before kick-off.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.0 goals. I lean slightly lower: Hamburg under Polzin have won games with around 35-37% possession and tight margins (1-0 against Stuttgart), and Schalke have scored little lately (0-0 at Köln, 0-2 at home to Leipzig, one late goal at Hoffenheim).

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners with Hamburg taking most of them. I lean a little lower because Polzin's Hamburg have been happy to sit compact without the ball, which tends to limit their own corner count at home against a side that may need to attack.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards. Schalke's position near the bottom adds some edge, but there is no referee named yet and nothing in the news points clearly up or down, so I stay with the number for now.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.5 shots. Hamburg's low-possession approach and Schalke's blunt recent attack both suggest a slightly quieter game than that, so I lean a touch lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target. With Schalke scoring once in their last three league games and Hamburg winning tight, low-margin games, I lean a little lower.
